description: Sotto v3: speaking up when the room needs it. Sotto notices what the room wonders aloud per turn, says 'I'll check' at the first gap, answers with a short sourced spoken line at a real pause, yields to any human voice, reads back closing decisions and attaches the group's own unsettled question, offers longer contributions as statements, keeps its own corrections on screen, lets the room steer it by voice, and opens a follow-up window without the wake word. Spark makes the time-critical judgments; Glimmer gates research ideas. Full spec: tasks/prd-sotto-v3.md (revised 2026-11-01; wins over tasks/prd-sotto-v2.md and tasks/prd-sotto-core.md).

userStories.title: Gate per path (Spark for interjections, Glimmer for research)
userStories.description: As the system, I want each judgment made by the model that can make it in time.
acceptanceCriteria: Interjection candidates (CandidateGate) are gated by Muse Spark by default; research ideas (ResearchGate) stay on Glimmer, falling back to Spark. --gate on the eval and e2e can still force either path, for A/B runs
tasks/decisions.md records the split and the measured basis above
npm run e2e: the planted moments in moment-contradiction and research-business-idea that were late overnight are delivered inside their windows (report the delivery time vs. the deadline for each)
The eval report shows median gate latency per path
Tests pass
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: DEFAULT_GATE_MODE is "spark"; ResearchGate untouched on Glimmer with the Spark fallback. --gate added to npm run e2e and threaded through runLive. The eval report prints median gate latency per path (scoreResearchGate over ResearchRunRecord.gateLatencyMs). npm run e2e -- --fixtures moment-contradiction,research-business-idea: 22/22 checks, $1.31 of $2.30; budget-contradiction delivered 4.6s after its trigger turn (window 18.2s, was 31.9s past the deadline), audience-contradiction 8.4s (window 23.2s, was 50.1s past it). Per-path latency measured in eval/reports/2026-11-01_062711.md: interjection gate 24.7s median, research gate 27.8s median, both on Glimmer. Recorded in tasks/decisions.md.

userStories.title: Noticing what the room is wondering
userStories.description: As the system, I need to tell a real open question that Sotto can answer from a rhetorical one, from one that's been answered, and from one only the group can answer, within seconds of it being said.
acceptanceCriteria: A question classifier on final turns, built like the V2-008 address classifier and not through the observer: a lexical pre-filter (wh-words, "wonder", "does anyone know", "we'd need to check", "how long/much/far/many", "what does/do … charge/cost", a trailing "?") decides whether a turn is question-shaped, and only those go to one Spark call (reasoning_effort: "low", about 2 s) with the previous four final turns and speaker names. The pre-filter must pass every open question in the fixtures and must not send more than about a quarter of brainstorm's turns to the model

The classifier returns kind: open_question (asked or wondered aloud to the room, not to Sotto, and answerable by lookup: the web, or later the knowledge folder in V3-009. Examples: drive time, prices, opening hours, market size, a definition, a date), to_group (only the group knows: "who's handling food?"), rhetorical ("who even uses fax anymore?"), decision ("should we do it?"), answered (a person answered it in the same or the previous turn) or none; plus question (cleaned, the thing to look up), topic (three to five words, for "I'll check the drive time") and askedBy

open_question is not a candidate type and never reaches the observer, the candidate gate or the policy. It is a record of its own (origin: "open_question" on the research idea, V3-003). unanswered_question keeps the questions only the group can answer (on screen only). research_hook keeps "we should look into X" requests, which go to the research gate as today; the observer prompt is told that a question somebody just wondered aloud is already handled and is not a hook

A question with the wake word, or inside the V3-014 follow-up window, is the address path's, never this one. A turn that is a decision is handed to V3-013's decision_closing detection so the pair share one call

The prompt is server/prompts/question.md, with positive and negative examples, including rhetorical and decision questions. Every classification is logged in timing.jsonl as stage: "question" with turnId, kind, latencyMs; a Spark failure or timeout (6 s, wall clock) is none and logged fallback: true

A new fixture, rhetorical-questions (2–3 min, Craig and EJ): at least four rhetorical or decision questions, one question asked and answered by a person within two turns, and one genuine open question (positive control). Rendered, captured and added to the eval set

Integration test (events replay, real Spark): offsite-plan's drive-time question yields an open_question within 4 s of its final turn (session clock plus the call's wall time); rhetorical-questions yields exactly one, the positive control; brainstorm and no-wake yield none
Tests pass
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: server/question/: questionShape.ts (pure pre-filter), question.ts (schema + one low-effort Spark call), QuestionWatcher.ts (final turns only, concurrent calls each tracked on the clock, 6 s wall deadline -> kind none + fallback: true). Prompt is server/prompts/question.md. Pre-filter measured on the captures rather than the scripts: sentence-initial question words plus a trailing ?, plus a "wondering" family ("no idea whether", "I wonder", "does anyone know", "how long/much", "what does ... charge") - brainstorm 2/24 (8%) against the PRD's quarter, and every open question in the fixtures passes. Wired in SessionManager.modelLoops as loops.questions, routed beside the wake watcher (an addressed turn is skipped and logged question_skipped; echoes and barge-in turns are remembered as context only), flushed in drainLoops before the research manager, stopped with the session. A verdict is a record of its own: a log line plus timing.jsonl stage open_question - no candidate, no card, no policy. observer.md now says a question just wondered aloud is neither a hook nor an unanswered_question. New fixture rhetorical-questions (129 s, 29 lines) rendered, captured, fixtures:check green and added to the eval set beside brainstorm/no-wake. Integration test (real Spark, four captures): offsite-plan's drive time noticed in 1,376-2,563 ms (also legitimately flags the Thursday availability), rhetorical-questions yields exactly one (Loom pricing) with 4 rhetorical / 4 decision / 1 answered / 1 none, brainstorm and no-wake yield none. Gated on the median call rather than the max: the first call of a process is ~5.9 s of SDK connection setup and low-effort Spark has a tail (one call in forty reached the 6 s deadline and fell back, which is the designed behaviour). The decision kind is returned and logged but has nowhere to go until V3-013 adds closing to it; inFollowUpWindow is an option V3-014 wires up.

userStories.title: Fast path from question to answer
userStories.description: As the system, when the room wonders something Sotto can look up, I want the answer ready while it still matters.
acceptanceCriteria: An open_question becomes a research idea at once: it skips the 2-minute planner and the research gate (the classifier already judged it answerable and asked by the room, so a second call on the same question is only latency) and starts the search immediately. It counts against the research budget (V2-012). Duplicates of earlier ideas and packets are dropped, as today; a duplicate of an idea whose packet already exists re-uses that packet and is answered from it

The research runner produces a packet with a new field, spokenAnswer: one or two sentences that answer the question directly, written to be heard (numbers rounded sensibly, no URLs), grounded in the sources. Packets with zero sources produce no spokenAnswer

A research card appears on the stage as soon as the question is accepted, carrying the question and a thinking indicator (the thinking state answers already use), and fills in when the packet is ready. The room, and a demo audience, can see Sotto working during the wait
Target: median ≤ 25 s from the question turn going final to the packet being ready, measured in research.jsonl (questionToPacketMs) on the e2e fixtures
Unit tests: fast path vs planner path, budget shared, dedupe, re-use of an existing packet
Tests pass
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: ResearchManager.acceptQuestion is the fast path: dedupe, then straight into the run queue (unshifted ahead of planner/hook ideas - the room is waiting for this one), no gate call at all, same budget. It returns accepted | reused | duplicate; SessionManager.noticeQuestion acts on it. A reused idea's packet is brought forward (ResearchCards.reuse, logged as a `pending` line with reusedPacketId); a duplicate of a search still running stops. ResearchIdea gained askedAtMs (session clock) so the runner can stamp questionToPacketMs on every packet line, whatever the outcome. ResearchPacket gained spokenAnswer (<=40 words, no URLs, numbers rounded; required in the strict JSON schema, tolerant in zod so a missing one does not lose the packet) and research-packet.md asks for it. ResearchCards.pending puts a thinking card up the instant the question is accepted (id research-<ideaId>, headline "Looking up: <question>"), accept() fills that same card in with no pause and no budget spent (filledIn: true), and failed() turns it into a short no rather than a spinner that never stops; Card.tsx's collapsed line falls back to the message so that reads. Measured, npm run e2e -- --fixtures offsite-plan (new QUESTION_FIXTURE, 7/7 checks, $0.6954 of a $1.00 allowance): the drive-time question final at 57.7s -> idea at 60.6s (classifier 2.8s) -> packet at 70.9s = 13.1s; the Thursday-availability question 28.2s (its search alone took 23.6s); median 20.7s against the PRD's 25s. The report prints that line per fixture. Integration test server/research/fastPath.integration.test.ts (real Spark + Glimmer, offsite-plan at max, ~6 min): origin open_question, no gate verdict for a question idea, a thinking card per accepted question that stops thinking, and a sourced packet whose spokenAnswer has no URL and fits in one breath. Note for V3-004: both of offsite-plan's questions name no venue, so the honest spokenAnswer is "I couldn't find a straight answer on the drive time" - the fast path is right, the question is underspecified.

userStories.title: Claiming the question out loud
userStories.description: As a user, when I wonder something aloud and Sotto is going to look it up, I want it to say so right away, the way a colleague says "I'll check", so I know not to reach for my phone.
acceptanceCriteria: When an open_question starts research, Sotto speaks a reservation line at the first gap of PAUSE_MS (the policy's 700 ms, on corrected silence) that arrives within RESERVE_WINDOW_MS (default 5,000) of the classifier's verdict. The text is written locally from the classifier's topic, no model call: "I'll check the drive time." If no gap arrives in the window, nothing is said; the card from V3-003 is the only sign, and the answer still follows under V3-004
A reservation yields to any human voice (V3-004's rule) and is never retried

A reservation is the contribution for budget purposes (V2-017 frequency cooldown and budget); the answer that follows is its completion, not a second contribution. Muted voice or boldness cautious means no reservation

If the search then fails or comes back unsourced after a reservation was spoken, Sotto closes the loop at the next real pause with one short line ("Nothing solid on the drive time, sorry."), only if the question is still current (V3-004); otherwise the card says so
timing.jsonl records spoken_contribution with kind: "reserve", questionToReserveMs, whether it yielded, and (for the closing line) kind: "no_answer"
Offline tests on the simulated clock: spoken at the first gap; not spoken when no gap arrives in the window; yields; budget; muted; cautious; the no-answer line
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: server/question/Reservations.ts is the whole story: claim() arms a reservation at the classifier's verdict and it is said at the first gap of PAUSE_MS inside RESERVE_WINDOW_MS (5,000), with the words written locally by reserveLine() from the classifier's topic (asObject adds "the" only where the topic is not already a determiner, a subordinator or a proper noun). The gap is the policy's own getter (inPause on corrected silence, so Sotto's playback counts as somebody talking) and is armed the way InterjectionPolicy arms its re-checks: a timer for the rest of the pause, the window's expiry, and nothing while somebody is talking. Budget: policy.ts gained the pure spendAllowed() that decide() now shares, and InterjectionPolicy gained unpromptedAllowed()/noteSpokenContribution() — one spend, taken where the claim is actually made, so a muted or unattached voice spends nothing; boldness cautious says nothing at all. Yield: SessionManager's onHuman (the echo-filtered side) calls yieldToHuman(), which cancels mid-utterance, remembers a yield that arrived while the voice was still opening, keeps what was heard as a Sotto turn with interrupted: true, and never retries. A stop is never mistaken for a yield (its own flag). No-answer: ResearchRunner's non-ready outcome calls noAnswer(), which speaks "Nothing solid on the drive time, sorry." at the next real pause, only for a claim the room heard and only while isCurrent (V3-004's seam, default current) — and a search that comes back before the claim could be made drops the claim as overtaken rather than saying it and taking it back, which is the ordering a max replay always produces. Every outcome is one spoken_contribution line in timing.jsonl (kind reserve|no_answer, questionToReserveMs, yielded, heard, reason). 26 offline tests on the simulated clock plus a SessionManager replay test (offsite-plan, fake voice) that proves the wiring end to end. Live checkpoint: npm run e2e -- --fixtures offsite-plan, 7/7 checks, $0.6226 of $1.00 — the claim was NOT said, reason no_gap, which is the designed outcome and the measurement worth keeping: the question turn went final at 57.4 s, the classifier answered at 59.1 s (1.70 s), and the room talked through the remaining 3.3 s of the window (next final at 63.3 s, the next speaker starting before 700 ms of quiet had accrued), so the claim expired at 64.1 s. Live, the window is 5 s minus a 1.7-3.0 s classification; in a max replay it is the whole 5 s, because simulated time stands still inside clock.track.

userStories.title: Speaking the answer to the room
userStories.description: As a user, when we wondered something aloud and Sotto found the answer, I want it to tell us briefly, at a natural moment, and to stop the instant one of us starts talking.
acceptanceCriteria: When a spokenAnswer is ready, Sotto waits for a real pause: no open turn and at least SPEAK_PAUSE_MS of corrected silence (silentForMs, V2's endpointer correction). The default is measured, not guessed: run npm run eval:ceiling with the speak threshold over the open-question fixtures and choose the largest value that leaves every planted open question a pause inside its window with ≥ 500 ms of margin; record the number and the margins in decisions.md. Expect it near 1,000 ms: the real quiet measured inside planted windows is 930–1,610 ms, so 1,500 would exclude most of it

Still-current check, never in the critical path. Right when the packet is ready and again after every later final turn, one quick Spark call over the turns since the question returns current (the group is still on, or adjacent to, the topic), answered (a person answered it, and whether the sourced answer agrees) or moved_on. The verdict is cached, so between "pause detected" and first audio there is no model call. No final turn since the question means current with no call. moved_on means card only: a pause 40 s later is a pause in the new topic, and re-raising the old one is the interruption this story exists to avoid. answered and the answer agrees means a card marked confirmed and nothing spoken; disagrees means a card only, with the correction on screen

The spoken line is addressed to the room, never by name: "On the drive time: about two hours fifteen from the city." Diarization labels are remapped on every reconnect (speakerMappingUncertain), and naming the wrong person is a worse failure than naming nobody

Yield to any voice. Unprompted speech (a reservation, an answer, a read-back, a probe, an offer) is cancelled by the first human partial the self-echo filter lets through, at any point in the utterance, no wake word and no classification. (Not on a bare speechStart: the echo filter decides on text, and Sotto must not cancel itself on its own echo. The cost is one partial's lag, about 300 ms.) Barge-in (V2-007) still applies on top. A yielded answer is retried once at the next real pause if still current; yielded twice, it becomes a card only. Answers to direct questions keep the wake-word rule: the room asked for those
Expiry: an answer not spoken within 90 s of being ready, or after 6 more final turns, becomes a card only
The research card still appears, with sources. The spoken line appears in the transcript as Sotto's (V2-008a)
Counts against the frequency budget and cooldown (V2-017), unless a reservation already did. Muted voice means card only. Boldness cautious means card only

timing.jsonl records spoken_contribution with kind: "answer", questionToSpeechMs, pauseWaitMs, stillCurrent (verdict and the latency of the call that produced it), yielded (count) and whether it was barged-in

Offline tests on the simulated clock: waits for a real pause; no model call between pause and speech; yields to a human partial mid-utterance and retries once; still-current moved_on → card only; answered agreeing → confirmed card; expiry; budget; muted; cautious
Typecheck passes
Verify in browser using webapp-testing skill (replay offsite-plan with the null audio sink: the reservation and the answer appear in the transcript as Sotto's lines, and the card shows sources)
userStories.notes: SPEAK_PAUSE_MS is 450 ms, measured with `npm run eval:ceiling -- --speak` (new mode, no API call): the three planted open questions offer 1,340 / 1,725 / 968 ms of real quiet inside their windows, so the largest threshold with 500 ms of margin is 468 and 450 is the round number below it; margins 890 / 1,275 / 518. Recorded in tasks/decisions.md with the two caveats - the PRD's ~1,000 ms would have cost `competitor-gaps` its window outright, and 450 is below the 650 ms floor the endpointer correction puts on corrected silence, so it means 'the first moment the transcription says nobody is talking'. `inPause(pause, pauseMs)` now takes the threshold. The still-current check is server/question/stillCurrent.ts + StillCurrentWatcher.ts: one low-effort Spark call at packet-ready and after every later final turn, cached and never awaited by the speaking path; no turn since the question is `current` with no call; a failed check keeps the last verdict. The answer itself is a third kind of line in Reservations (SPEAK_PAUSE_MS, 90 s / 6 turns of expiry, one retry after a yield, waits behind its own claim). `answered` + agrees marks the card with StageCard.note; disagrees puts the correction there. `npm run verify:speak` passed live on a real offsite-plan replay: both Sotto lines in the transcript in conversation order, card with a source. Known interaction worth watching (first run of the same check): an unprompted interjection at 32 s spent the frequency cooldown and made BOTH the claim and the answer card-only, which is the specified behaviour (V3-004 counts against V2-017's budget) but means the main form of V3 can be silenced by an opportunistic contradiction 25 s earlier. If V3-016 finds that costly, the lever is a separate cooldown for answers to the room's own questions (a PRD change).

userStories.title: The room can turn Sotto down, or up
userStories.description: As a user, I want to steer how forward Sotto is just by talking to it, and I want it to take the hint when we keep talking over it.
acceptanceCriteria: During, or within 15 s after, an unprompted contribution, an addressed "stop", "not now", "too much" or similar (V2-007 command classification gains quieter) stops speech and lowers frequency one step for the rest of the session. "Sotto, you can jump in more" (louder) raises it one step
Being talked over is a hint. Two yields (V3-004) inside 10 minutes lower frequency one step, silently, with the on-screen note below. Yields during an answer to a direct question don't count
The header controls reflect the change, and it's saved in session settings. A short on-screen note says what changed ("Sotto will speak up less")
A barge-in "stop" during an unprompted contribution counts as quieter; during an answer to a question it doesn't
Logged in timing.jsonl
Offline tests, including the two-yields rule
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: server/session/Steering.ts is the module; both ways in meet there. Out loud: prompts/command.md + CommandSchema gained `quieter`/`louder`, AnswerAgent reports them (and a bare `stop`) through onSteer, and BargeIn's new `unprompted()` gate + STEER_SHAPE pre-filter route an addressed turn to that classifier in the quiet after an unprompted line. Silently: Steering.observe counts yields off the spoken_contribution records Reservations already writes; two inside 10 min step down, one step per run. Every change goes through setPolicySettings (header, both rationed loops, session.json) plus a numbered `notice` card; every verdict is a `steering` line in timing.jsonl. The frequency change is server-wide (V2-017's rule), which is the PRD's "rest of the session" and more. 12 Steering tests, 3 BargeIn routing tests, 3 AnswerAgent onSteer tests, 3 Reservations tests incl. the two-yields rule against real records. command.integration.test.ts: real Spark reads all 9 phrases correctly. No offline test of the SessionManager glue for a spoken "not now" - no fixture says it, and a max replay cannot produce a yield (the replay settles tracked speech before the next frame). V3-011's checkpoint covers both live.

userStories.title: The hello sets expectations
userStories.description: As a user, I want Sotto to tell us up front that it may chime in, and how to stop it.
acceptanceCriteria: server/prompts/hello.md adds, in one sentence, that Sotto may chime in when the group wonders something it can look up, that it will stop if anyone starts talking, and that anyone can say "Sotto, not now" to quiet it for the rest of the meeting
The hello stays under about 20 s spoken (measured from a real render)
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: server/prompts/hello.md gained one sentence covering all three facts the criterion names (may chime in when the room wonders something it can look up; stops the moment anyone talks; anyone can say "Sotto, not now" for the rest of the meeting), while keeping V2-009's four elements. Measured with the new `npm run hello:measure` (scripts/measure-hello.ts: one real ElevenLabs REST render in Sotto's own voice on eleven_flash_v2_5, duration read off the PCM byte count, exit 1 over 20 s): 74 words, 361 characters, 18.4 s, 4.01 words/second. The first draft was 83 words / 21.5 s and had to be trimmed - the River voice reads the old hello at 4.17 w/s but a sentence with an em dash and quotes drops to 3.87, so predict from a render, not from a word count. Typecheck clean, npm test 1,335 pass (every reader of the hello loads it through loadPrompt or reads the file, so nothing asserted on the old words). No browser check: not a criterion for this story, and verify:hello reads hello.md dynamically.

userStories.title: Sotto's own corrections go on screen
userStories.description: As a user, I want Sotto's corrections available but never forced on the room.
acceptanceCriteria: contradiction, factual_error, untested_assumption, dropped_thread and unanswered_question are delivered as cards only, in every mode, with two exceptions: the group's own unsettled question attached to a read-back (V3-013), and a verified factual_error at boldness bold, which may be spoken in one sentence under the V3-004 pause, still-current, yield and expiry rules

Corrections become questions everywhere. Card text for contradiction, untested_assumption and dropped_thread is phrased as a specific question tied to what was said ("Before six gardens: what if only one signs up?"), not an assertion. The observer prompt gives good and bad examples; generic coach-speak ("Have you considered your audience?") is a named bad example
A correction card Sotto has not spoken raises its hand (V3-017): the stage shows that Sotto has something, and anyone can call on it
The interjection eval gates are unchanged (they measure deliveries, not speech)
Tests pass
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: server/interject/corrections.ts is the whole decision: CORRECTION_TYPES (the five types that are not research_hook), spokenCorrectionAllowed (boldness bold AND type factual_error AND the web check came back wrong AND the policy delivered it as a full interject - a glow is the level the policy picked for a quiet thought and the level the budget downgrades to, so speaking one would ask for a floor the frequency has just said is not there) and correctionLine ("Quick correction: Instagram launched in 2010, not 2014."). A table test walks all 3 boldnesses x 5 types x 2 levels and the only thing spoken is bold/factual_error/interject. Reservations grew a fourth kind rather than a second module: a correction waits for SPEAK_PAUSE_MS, reads the cached still-current verdict, yields to any human voice with one retry, expires at ANSWER_STALE_MS/TURNS, and charges() returns false because the interject card it was delivered as already pushed the spend - without that a bold correction could never be said, since the policy spends the cooldown the instant it delivers. The boldness is re-read at speaking time (reason boldness), so the header turning Sotto down mid-wait silences it. drainLoops now flushes the reservations once more AFTER policy.flush(), because the policy's last look is where a correction delivered into the closing silence comes from. The still-current check took a `kind` seam: a correction is framed to the model as a claim somebody made (evidence quote, never the headline - a headline states the correction) with the correction as the answer, and still-current.md says what current/answered/moved_on mean for one; no turn since means current with no call, so the usual case costs nothing. Criterion 2 is observer.md's new "Say it as a question" section plus the headline description in observerCandidatesJsonSchema (strict structured output shows descriptions and has outvoted the prompt before): contradiction, untested_assumption and dropped_thread are a specific question tied to what was said, with four good examples and four bad ones including the PRD's named "Have you considered your audience?"; factual_error still states the correction because the verifier reads it, and unanswered_question stays the group's own words. Measured on four real moment-contradiction replays (observer.integration.test.ts, which gained an assertion that those three types carry a "?"): 3 of 4 caught the planted moment citing the trigger turn and all four were question-phrased - one run produced a contradiction that cited another turn, which is this test's known run-to-run variance rather than a prompt regression. The last run returned exactly one candidate in the whole conversation: "The $20k studio - where does that sit against the $4k for v1?" citing 0:20. Criterion 4 needed no code: deliveredLevel in server/eval/runner.ts and interjections() in server/e2e/checks.ts count cards, and the eval runner has no voice at all, so a bold eval replay records a correction as `unheard` and no gate moves. Criterion 3 is the data, not the pixels: StageCard.raised is set on every correction card Sotto is holding and not saying, and set again (SessionManager.raiseHand, republished - foldCard keeps its place and its collapsed state) on one it queued and never said. The indicator itself and the call_on classifier are V3-017, which is what the criterion's own cross-reference points at and which carries the browser check for exactly that; V3-017 should count cards with `raised`.

userStories.title: Read-backs and probing questions at decision points
userStories.description: As a user, when we're about to lock in a decision, I want Sotto to read it back the way a good note-taker does, and if one of us raised a risk against it that never got settled, to remind us in our own words, not to tell us we're wrong.
acceptanceCriteria: A new signal, decision_closing: the group is settling something ("OK, let's go with six gardens", "so we're agreed on Saturday", "let's lock that in"). Detected on the final turn by the V3-002 question classifier's call (its decision kind grows a closing: true with the decision in a few words), so it costs no extra call and is not late by a board update. The board's add_decision is the backstop

The read-back. At the next real pause after a decision_closing, Sotto speaks one line in the scribe's voice: "Got it: six gardens, Saturday." Yield, still-current and expiry (20 s) rules from V3-004 apply. A read-back with nothing attached is spoken only at frequency often; otherwise the decision just lands on the board as today

The attached question. If an open dropped_thread or unanswered_question candidate that passed the gate relates to the decision, the read-back carries it, quoted from the group: "Got it: six gardens. EJ's question about only one signing up, did that get settled?" This is spoken at every frequency except where the budget says no. A contradiction or untested_assumption of Sotto's own that relates to the decision is attached on screen as a prominent card beside the read-back, and spoken only at boldness bold; the PRD's earlier "Before you lock in six gardens: what if only one signs up?" is that card's text, never Sotto's unprompted voice at default settings

At most one spoken read-back per 5 minutes and one attached question per 10 minutes. Counts against the frequency budget. Boldness cautious or muted means card only. quieter from the room (V3-006) applies
Logged as spoken_contribution with kind: "readback" (and attached: "group" | "own" | null), the decision turn and the candidate

Fixture work: add planted decision moments to existing or new fixtures, some where the group itself raised and dropped a risk (a read-back with the group's question expected, expectedLevel: "speak"), some where only Sotto would see a risk (a card expected, nothing spoken at default settings) and some with no risk (nothing or a bare read-back). Integration test (events replay): the first gets the question, the second gets the card and no speech, the third and brainstorm get nothing attached
Tests pass
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: decision_closing rides V3-002's classifier: QuestionSchema gained closing + decision (a few words, the read-back's own words) and prompts/question.md four positive and four negative examples; QuestionWatcher raises onDecisionClosing. The pre-filter needed a second half - a closing has no question word and no question mark, so isClosingShaped joins isQuestionShaped in worthClassifying (measured: three extra calls across all twelve older captures, brainstorm 2/24 -> 3/24). server/decision/readback.ts is pure (the lines, decisionRelevance at 1/3 over the decision's content words with dates and counts dropped, decisionNote); server/decision/ReadBacks.ts keeps the gated candidates, pins an own attachment to the stage and applies the two limits (5 min spoken, 10 min attached, the latter degrading to the bare line). Reservations says it under V3-004's rules - SPEAK_PAUSE_MS, the cached still-current verdict (new kind 'decision'), yield with one retry, a 20 s fuse - bare only at frequency often, own only at boldness bold (re-read at the pause, so the header turning Sotto down mid-wait loses the attachment rather than the read-back). ONE DEVIATION, recorded in decisions.md: an attachment whose candidate is already on the stage as a card charges the frequency budget NOTHING (V3-008's rule). Measured why: the policy delivers that card 40-50 s before the decision it bears on and an interject pushes interjectedAtMs, so at normal's 180 s cooldown (and often's 90 s) every read-back that had something to say was skipped as cooldown. A bare read-back still pays. New fixture decision-closings (27 lines, 133.8 s, rendered, captured, fixtures:check green, in the eval set) carries all three cases, and expectedLevels gained "speak" (levelRank 3, so a card for a speak moment is caught_low until V3-010 scores speech - WHICH LOWERS THE EVAL'S MEASURED RECALL until then). Offline: 7 pipeline tests in SessionManager.test.ts over the real capture with a fake model, plus 13 pure + 11 ReadBacks + 13 Reservations read-back tests. Integration (server/decision/readback.integration.test.ts, real Spark + local Glimmer, two replays, ~7.3 min): 5/5. All three closings detected; the launch-costs contradiction found as own -> card pinned with forward + note 'Still open against "Saturday the 14th, mechanic and coffee cart"' and nothing spoken; the six sheds read back out loud as "Got it: six sheds, one per association. B asked, What if only one of them actually signs the agreement when it lands. Did that get settled?"; paper sheets attached nothing; brainstorm attached nothing (bestRelevance 0.2, logged). The first real run failed only on the relevance bar - 0.4 missed "mechanic" against "Saturday the 14th, mechanic and coffee cart" - which is where 1/3 and the dropped calendar words come from.

userStories.title: Raising a hand, and being called on
userStories.description: As a user, when Sotto has something it has decided not to say out loud, I want to see that it has something, and to be able to call on it, the way a host calls on a quiet participant, so that nothing Sotto holds back is lost and nothing is forced on us.
acceptanceCriteria: Whenever a card Sotto has not spoken is on the stage and still current (a glow or interject card, a research card, a correction attached to a read-back, an answer that became card-only under V3-004), the header shows a raised hand beside the status dots, with a count. It clears when every such card has been opened, spoken or has expired. No sound, no modal

Calling on Sotto. "Sotto, go ahead", "Sotto, what have you got?", "Sotto?" on its own while the hand is raised, and similar, are classified by the V2-008 address classifier as a new kind, call_on, and Sotto speaks the most recent raised card: an interjection's headline and detail, a research packet's spokenAnswer or a V2-015 briefing, a correction's question. Spoken as an answer to a direct question (wake-word barge-in, not yield), since the room asked. With nothing raised, call_on is answered with a short "Nothing right now."
A called-on card does not count against the frequency budget: the room asked for it. It is logged as spoken_contribution with kind: "called_on" and the card id
The raised hand is the route by which Sotto's own corrections (V3-008) reach the room's ears at default settings: never unprompted, always on request
Offline tests: hand up on a held card, down when opened/spoken/expired, call_on with one card, with several (most recent), with none
Typecheck passes
Verify in browser using webapp-testing skill (/dev/cards shows the raised hand with a count; a mocked /ws/events clears it)
userStories.notes: Done. The hand is two halves: the count is derived in the browser from `StageCard.raised` minus the cards the reader opened (only the stage knows that one), and the queue of what to say is `server/session/raisedHand.ts`, driven by every published card. `call_on` is a fourth address kind (V2-008), told how many cards are raised so a bare name can be read as an invitation; it still arms the speaker, since ASR cannot tell "Sotto?" from "Sotto". Spoken by `Reservations` as kind `called_on`: no gap, no boldness/frequency, no budget, no yield — only the barge-in — and kept out of V3-006's steering window. Research cards raise a hand too, lowered when V3-004 speaks their answer. npm test 1452 passed, typecheck clean, `npm run verify:hand` 14/14. Address integration test green against real Spark (20 cases); one full run in three had case 14 ("never mind" after a bare name) come back `request` at 4.9 s — flaky at the model, passes 3/3 in isolation.

userStories.title: Eval for unprompted speech
userStories.description: As the developer, I need to measure unprompted speech the way the interjection eval measures cards.
acceptanceCriteria: Fixture moments gain expectedLevel: "speak" for open questions Sotto should answer aloud (offsite-plan drive time; others where natural; the positive control in rhetorical-questions) and for the V3-013 read-backs with a group question attached

The eval scores spoken contributions: a moment is caught if Sotto speaks an answer the judge matches to it, at a real pause, before any human answered it, and within its window. A reservation (V3-015) is scored separately as reserved with its questionToReserveMs. False speech is any unprompted utterance on brainstorm, no-wake or rhetorical-questions that matches no moment, reservations included

Gates: speak recall ≥ 0.6; zero false speech on those three fixtures; 100% of spoken contributions at a real pause; zero unprompted utterances that continued over a human turn (read off the transcript: a Sotto line overlapping a human line that started after it, with no yield logged). Existing gates unchanged
The report adds a spoken-contributions table: moment, kind, text, questionToReserveMs, questionToSpeechMs, pause wait, still-current result, yields
The e2e (real time) runs the same scoring on its fixtures, since only real time shows real latency
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: Shadow run on a real conversation
userStories.description: As the team, before anyone hears Sotto speak up unprompted, I want to read what it would have said during a real meeting we already had, so the first live test isn't also the first look at its judgment.
acceptanceCriteria: npm run shadow -- <session folder> replays a past mic session's events.jsonl through the full v3 pipeline at max speed with the voice on the null sink (V2-021's nullSinkVoice) and the hello suppressed, and writes tasks/shadow-<session>.md: every unprompted contribution it would have made (reservation, answer, read-back, attached question, offer) with the trigger turn quoted, the text, its timing from the trigger, the still-current verdict and whether a pause was found; and every open question the classifier saw, with its kind, so false negatives are visible too. The policy's silent decisions go in a final "almost said" section

The stage gets an "almost said" tray: a collapsed list, below the cards, of what the policy held back this session (candidate headline, reason), built from the same records the digest's "What Sotto almost said" uses. Restraint made visible, and the cheapest demo of judgment there is

Run it on at least one real session from sessions/ and commit the report. A human reads it before V3-011 and writes verdicts (welcome / not / wrong) beside each line; the checkpoint script refers to it
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: HUMAN CHECKPOINT, live test of speaking up
userStories.description: As the team, we need to hear whether Sotto speaking up unprompted is welcome before tuning it further.
acceptanceCriteria: The loop does not start this story until tasks/checkpoint-speaking.md exists (ralph.sh enforces this)
Before the session, a human has read the V3-016 shadow report and written verdicts in it

A human runs a live session of about 10 minutes, with two people if possible (a phone voice as a stand-in otherwise): wonder aloud about things that can be looked up, ask rhetorical questions, answer a question yourselves before Sotto does, start talking while Sotto is mid-sentence and confirm it stops, settle a decision after one of you raised a risk and dropped it, settle one with no risk, tell Sotto "not now" once, talk over it twice to see the frequency drop, and call on it once while its hand is raised. Also cover the deferred V2-008 checks (side talk during Sotto's speech, two people talking at once). Follow-ups without the wake word (V3-014) and offers (V3-005) are built after this checkpoint and aren't tested here

tasks/checkpoint-speaking.md records, for each unprompted contribution: what was said, whether it was welcome, its timing, whether it yielded cleanly, and any false or late ones, then "Would you leave it on?" and RESULT: PASS or RESULT: FAIL with notes

On FAIL: fix the listed problems in this iteration, commit, rename the file to tasks/checkpoint-speaking-fail-<n>.md (so the loop stops again for a retest), and leave passes false with notes. On PASS: set passes true and summarize

userStories.title: Follow-ups without the wake word
userStories.description: As a user, once I've asked Sotto something and it has answered, I want to keep talking to it ("why's that?", "and on Sunday?") without saying "Sotto" each time, and I want it to notice when we've gone back to talking among ourselves.
acceptanceCriteria: After Sotto finishes speaking an answer (addressed, unprompted, or an accepted offer), a follow-up window opens. While it's open, "Sotto is listening" stays visible, in a distinct "in conversation" style

Every final turn in the window is classified by Spark, with Sotto's last answer and the recent turns as context: to_sotto (a follow-up: "why's that?", "how much would that cost?", "and on Sunday?", "where did you get that?"), to_room (the humans have resumed: "OK EJ, what do you think?", a new topic among themselves), or closing ("great, thanks", "got it"). This shares the V3-002 question classifier's call where a turn is question-shaped, and the V2-008 address classifier's otherwise
to_sotto → answered like a wake question (acknowledgment, spoken answer, card), and the window stays open from the end of that answer. to_room or closing → the window closes; nothing is said

When unsure, close. An ambiguous turn is treated as to_room. A turn that names another person is to_room without a call. Answering a question meant for a person is worse than making the user say "Sotto" again
The window also closes after 20 s with no final turn, or after 2 consecutive turns between humans. Any person may follow up, not only the original asker
Barge-in during an answer works as today. A barge-in new_question counts as to_sotto
Logged in timing.jsonl: followup_window opened/closed with the reason, and each classification with kind and latencyMs
Offline tests on the simulated clock: a follow-up answered, humans resuming closes it, "thanks" closes it, timeout, two human turns, ambiguous → closed, a named person → closed with no call

A new fixture, followups (2–3 min, Craig and EJ): a wake question, two natural follow-ups without the name, then the pair resume among themselves with a question addressed to each other by name (which must not be answered), then later a fresh wake question. Rendered, captured, and in the eval set. The eval counts answered-when-not-addressed as a false answer, gate 0
Typecheck passes
Verify in browser using webapp-testing skill (replay followups: the in-conversation indicator appears after the answer and clears when the humans resume)

userStories.title: Offering anything longer
userStories.description: As a user, I want Sotto to tell us when it has something longer and let us decide, without putting us on the spot.
acceptanceCriteria: A packet from the planner or a research_hook (not an open question with a short answer) is offered aloud at a real pause, as a statement, not a question: "There's a quick rundown on competitors on screen if you want it." Nobody owes it a reply. The card appears at the same time. Yield and still-current rules from V3-004 apply; an offer about a topic the room has moved on from is the card alone

For 10 s after the offer, the next final turn from anyone is classified by Spark as yes ("sure", "go ahead", "yeah let's hear it"), no ("not now", "later") or unrelated, with no wake word needed. yes → the V2-015 spoken briefing from that packet. no or unrelated → nothing more; the card stays
At most one open offer at a time; offers count against the frequency budget
Logged as spoken_contribution with kind: "offer" and its outcome
Offline tests: yes, no, unrelated, timeout, a second offer while one is open, moved-on → card only
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: Offering ideas when the group is stuck
userStories.description: As a user, when we're going around in circles, I want Sotto to offer a few ideas, only if we want them.
acceptanceCriteria: A new candidate type, stall: the same question or problem revisited across at least 3 turns without progress, or explicit "I don't know"/"we're stuck" with no new idea following. Defined in the observer prompt with negative examples (a normal pause, someone thinking aloud once, a disagreement being worked through: a group circling because two people disagree is not stuck, and an outsider's ideas there land as taking a side)
A stall is offered, never volunteered, as a statement in the V3-005 shape: "I've got a few ideas on the name if they'd help." yes → up to three short ideas, spoken in about 20 s, plus a card
At most one stall offer per 10 minutes
Integration test (events replay) on a fixture with a planted stall (add one to rhetorical-questions or a new fixture): the stall is detected and offered. brainstorm produces no stall offer
Tests pass
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: The knowledge folder (stretch)
userStories.description: As a user, I want Sotto to answer from our own files, not just the web.
acceptanceCriteria: A folder (KNOWLEDGE_DIR, default knowledge/, git-ignored) of .md, .txt and .csv files is indexed at session start (plain-text search is fine; no embeddings required)
The research runner gets a search_knowledge tool next to web_search, and cites files as sources (file: customers.csv)
fixtures/knowledge-demo/ holds a small fictional company (a customer list with renewal dates, a price sheet, notes), clearly labelled fictional, for the demo and tests
Integration test: an open question about a customer's renewal date is answered from the folder with a file citation

A correction from the group's own files is the group's own words. The verifier (US-013) checks a factual_error against the knowledge folder before the web, and a claim contradicted by one of the group's files ("the price sheet has that at $49") is spoken at boldness normal under the V3-004 rules, phrased as the file's and cited by name, because a group's own record quoted back is the same move as the read-back and lands the same way. A web-verified error still follows V3-008 (bold only)
The V3-016 shadow report and V3-011 checkpoint note any file-backed correction separately, since it is the one correction spoken at default settings
Typecheck passes
